newsitem.title: JAPAN: JGB rally seen fuelled by new buying after April.
newsitem.headline: JGB rally seen fuelled by new buying after April.

text.p: New investment backed by a view that interest rates won't be raised anytime soon is likely to keep fuelling a rally in Japanese government bonds (JGBs) after April 1, fund managers and traders said on Friday.

Among the extra cash that is emerging: over four trillion yen from maturing JGBs in June, and the Housing Loan Administration Corp's loan repayment of 1.2 trillion yen to agricultural financial bodies at the end of March.
A large part of these liquidity-conscious new funds is expected to be invested in JGBs, they said.

"The JGB market is likely to retain its firmness until late May, when economic data for April is released," said Yorinobu Hara, senior deputy general manager at the trading and sales department at Asahi Securities Co.

The five-day rally in JGBs this week was mainly attributed to cash bond purchases by Japanese banks and life insurers ahead of the business year-end. JGBs to be traded on and after March 21 are settled in the new year.

But even after April 1, the market may stay buoyant on concerns over the economy's fragile recovery and because higher demand and a lower-than-usual supply of long-term bonds are expected, fund managers and traders said.
"By late May, it is highly likely that the key June futures contract will hit 128.00 and the yield of the benchmark 182nd 10-year JGB will dip to two percent," Asahi's Hara said.
Some operators expect the market to enter a downtrend only after August, when major economic data for the April-June period will be released, he added.
The key June JGB futures contract finished Friday at 126.70 against Thursday's 126.25 close.
The yield of the key 182nd 10-year JGB hit an intra-day record low of 2.190 percent on Friday. The yield has been renewing record lows every day since Tuesday this week.

A senior fund manager at a Japanese life insurance company said he expected the yield of benchmark 10-year JGBs to fluctuate in a wide range of between 2.1 and 2.4 percent in the next couple of months.

"It is possible that the key bond yield will fall below the current record low levels because a lack of bearish factors due to expected weakness in the economic recovery is likely to encourage investors to increase JGB buying," he said.

There was a widespread view that the Bank of Japan (BOJ) would not tighten credit in the near future as the economic recovery this year is expected to be anaemic due to fiscal tightening from April 1.
The BOJ's "tankan" quarterly corporate survey due on April 2 is unlikely to show a bright picture for the economic recovery, the fund mangers and traders said.
Economic data for the period after Japan's consumption tax rises to five percent on April 1 will be unveiled only after late May.
Also, supply-demand conditions in the April-June period are expected to be more favourable than a year ago.

The amount of privately placed municipal bonds, issues of which usually peak between March and May, could be about five trillion yen in the March-May period this year, some 1.5 trillion yen smaller than a year earlier, they said.
